metadata.title: Latent Dirichlet Allocation
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF→text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Word
nodes.statement: A word is the basic unit of discrete data, an item from a vocabulary indexed by $\{1,\ldots,V\}$, represented as a unit-basis vector $w$ with $w^v = 1$ and $w^u = 0$ for $u \neq v$.
nodes.statement_clean: A word is a one-hot V-dimensional indicator vector picking out one item of the vocabulary.

nodes.name: Document
nodes.statement: A document is a sequence of $N$ words denoted by $\mathbf{w} = (w_1, w_2, \ldots, w_N)$, where $w_n$ is the $n$th word in the sequence.

nodes.name: Corpus
nodes.statement: A corpus is a collection of $M$ documents denoted by $\mathcal{D} = \{\mathbf{w}_1, \mathbf{w}_2, \ldots, \mathbf{w}_M\}$.

nodes.name: Dirichlet distribution
nodes.statement: A $k$-dimensional Dirichlet random variable $\theta$ on the $(k-1)$-simplex with parameter $\alpha$ has density $p(\theta\mid\alpha) = \frac{\Gamma(\sum_i \alpha_i)}{\prod_i \Gamma(\alpha_i)} \theta_1^{\alpha_1-1}\cdots\theta_k^{\alpha_k-1}$.

nodes.name: Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) generative model
nodes.statement: LDA generates each document by: (1) choose $N \sim \mathrm{Poisson}(\xi)$; (2) choose $\theta \sim \mathrm{Dir}(\alpha)$; (3) for each of $N$ words: choose topic $z_n \sim \mathrm{Multinomial}(\theta)$, then choose $w_n \sim p(w_n\mid z_n,\beta)$.
nodes.statement_clean: LDA defines a three-level generative process where documents are mixtures over topics drawn from a Dirichlet prior, and each word is drawn from a topic-conditional multinomial.

nodes.name: Exchangeability
nodes.statement: A finite set of random variables $\{z_1,\ldots,z_N\}$ is exchangeable if for any permutation $\pi$, $p(z_1,\ldots,z_N) = p(z_{\pi(1)},\ldots,z_{\pi(N)})$. An infinite sequence is infinitely exchangeable if every finite subsequence is exchangeable.

nodes.name: Word simplex and topic simplex
nodes.statement: The word simplex is the $(V-1)$-simplex of distributions over the vocabulary; the topic simplex is the sub-simplex spanned by $k$ chosen points (topics) on the word simplex.

nodes.name: Variational distribution for LDA
nodes.statement: The variational family $q(\theta, z\mid\gamma,\phi) = q(\theta\mid\gamma)\prod_{n=1}^N q(z_n\mid\phi_n)$, with Dirichlet parameter $\gamma$ and multinomial parameters $\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_N$, obtained by removing the edges between $\theta$, $z$ and $w$.

nodes.name: Smoothed LDA
nodes.statement: Smoothed LDA treats $\beta$ as a $k\times V$ random matrix whose rows are independently drawn from an exchangeable Dirichlet with scalar parameter $\eta$, and the joint variational posterior factorizes as $q(\beta_{1:k}, z_{1:M}, \theta_{1:M}\mid \lambda, \phi, \gamma) = \prod_{i=1}^k \mathrm{Dir}(\beta_i\mid\lambda_i)\prod_{d=1}^M q_d(\theta_d, z_d\mid\phi_d, \gamma_d)$.

nodes.name: Perplexity
nodes.statement: For a test set of $M$ documents, $\mathrm{perplexity}(\mathcal{D}_{\text{test}}) = \exp\bigl(-\sum_{d=1}^M \log p(\mathbf{w}_d) \big/ \sum_{d=1}^M N_d\bigr)$; lower perplexity means better generalization.

nodes.name: de Finetti representation theorem
nodes.statement: The joint distribution of an infinitely exchangeable sequence of random variables can be written as a mixture: there exists a distribution on a latent parameter $\theta$ such that the variables are conditionally i.i.d. given $\theta$.
conclusions: $p(z_1,\ldots,z_N) = \int p(\theta) \prod_{n=1}^N p(z_n\mid\theta)\, d\theta$ for some distribution on $\theta$

nodes.name: Joint distribution under LDA
nodes.statement: $p(\theta, \mathbf{z}, \mathbf{w}\mid\alpha,\beta) = p(\theta\mid\alpha)\prod_{n=1}^N p(z_n\mid\theta) p(w_n\mid z_n,\beta)$.

nodes.name: Marginal document likelihood
nodes.statement: $p(\mathbf{w}\mid\alpha,\beta) = \int p(\theta\mid\alpha) \Bigl(\prod_{n=1}^N \sum_{z_n} p(z_n\mid\theta) p(w_n\mid z_n,\beta)\Bigr) d\theta$.

nodes.name: Posterior over latent variables
nodes.statement: $p(\theta, \mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{w},\alpha,\beta) = p(\theta,\mathbf{z},\mathbf{w}\mid\alpha,\beta) / p(\mathbf{w}\mid\alpha,\beta)$; intractable due to the coupling between $\theta$ and $\beta$ in the topic summation.

nodes.name: KL-minimization for variational parameters
nodes.statement: $(\gamma^*, \phi^*) = \arg\min_{(\gamma,\phi)} D\bigl(q(\theta,\mathbf{z}\mid\gamma,\phi) \,\|\, p(\theta,\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{w},\alpha,\beta)\bigr)$.

nodes.name: Variational update equations
nodes.statement: $\phi_{ni} \propto \beta_{i w_n}\exp\{E_q[\log\theta_i\mid\gamma]\}$ and $\gamma_i = \alpha_i + \sum_{n=1}^N \phi_{ni}$, with $E_q[\log\theta_i\mid\gamma] = \Psi(\gamma_i) - \Psi\bigl(\sum_{j=1}^k \gamma_j\bigr)$.

nodes.name: M-step update for beta
nodes.statement: $\beta_{ij} \propto \sum_{d=1}^M \sum_{n=1}^{N_d} \phi^*_{dni} w_{dn}^j$.

nodes.name: Variational lower bound
nodes.statement: $\log p(\mathbf{w}\mid\alpha,\beta) = \mathcal{L}(\gamma,\phi;\alpha,\beta) + D\bigl(q(\theta,\mathbf{z}\mid\gamma,\phi)\,\|\,p(\theta,\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{w},\alpha,\beta)\bigr)$, where $\mathcal{L}$ is the Jensen-derived lower bound.

nodes.name: Dirichlet log-expectation identity
nodes.statement: If $\theta\sim\mathrm{Dir}(\alpha)$, then $E[\log\theta_i\mid\alpha] = \Psi(\alpha_i) - \Psi\bigl(\sum_{j=1}^k \alpha_j\bigr)$, where $\Psi$ is the digamma function.

nodes.name: Linear-time Newton-Raphson with rank-one Hessian
nodes.statement: If the Hessian has the form $H = \mathrm{diag}(h) + \mathbf{1} z \mathbf{1}^T$, then $H^{-1}g$ can be computed component-wise as $(H^{-1}g)_i = (g_i - c)/h_i$ with $c = \sum_j g_j/h_j \big/ (z^{-1} + \sum_j h_j^{-1})$, yielding linear-time Newton-Raphson.

nodes.name: Variational inference for LDA
nodes.statement: Coordinate-ascent fixed-point iteration that updates $\phi$ and $\gamma$ to minimize the KL divergence between the mean-field $q(\theta,\mathbf{z}\mid\gamma,\phi)$ and the true posterior $p(\theta,\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{w},\alpha,\beta)$.
output: Optimized variational parameters $\gamma^*$, $\phi^*$ approximating the document posterior
nodes.pseudocode: (1) initialize $\phi^0_{ni} := 1/k$ for all $i, n$; (2) initialize $\gamma_i := \alpha_i + N/k$ for all $i$; (3) repeat: for $n=1..N$, for $i=1..k$: $\phi^{t+1}_{ni} := \beta_{i w_n}\exp(\Psi(\gamma^t_i))$; normalize $\phi^{t+1}_n$; $\gamma^{t+1} := \alpha + \sum_n \phi^{t+1}_n$; until convergence.

nodes.name: Variational EM for LDA parameter estimation
nodes.statement: Alternating empirical-Bayes EM that maximizes the variational lower bound on the marginal log likelihood, alternating an E-step (variational inference per document) with an M-step (update $\alpha$ and $\beta$).
nodes.pseudocode: Repeat: (E-step) for each document $d$, run variational inference to obtain $(\gamma^*_d, \phi^*_d)$; (M-step) update $\beta_{ij} \propto \sum_d \sum_n \phi^*_{dni} w^j_{dn}$, update $\alpha$ via linear-time Newton-Raphson on the bound. Until lower bound converges.

nodes.name: Derivation of variational update equations
nodes.statement: Bound $\log p(\mathbf{w}\mid\alpha,\beta)$ via Jensen's inequality, expand the bound in $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\phi$, then maximize term-by-term in $\phi_{ni}$ (with simplex Lagrange multiplier) and in $\gamma_i$, recovering Eqs. (6) and (7).

nodes.name: Apply Jensen's inequality
nodes.statement: Write $\log p(\mathbf{w}\mid\alpha,\beta) = \log \int \sum_z p(\theta,\mathbf{z},\mathbf{w}\mid\alpha,\beta) d\theta$; multiply and divide by $q(\theta,\mathbf{z})$ inside the integral and apply Jensen to get $\log p(\mathbf{w}\mid\alpha,\beta) \geq E_q[\log p(\theta,\mathbf{z},\mathbf{w}\mid\alpha,\beta)] - E_q[\log q(\theta,\mathbf{z})]$.

nodes.name: Identify the slack as KL divergence
nodes.statement: The gap between $\log p(\mathbf{w}\mid\alpha,\beta)$ and the lower bound $\mathcal{L}(\gamma,\phi;\alpha,\beta)$ equals $D(q(\theta,\mathbf{z}\mid\gamma,\phi)\|p(\theta,\mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{w},\alpha,\beta))$, so maximizing the bound is equivalent to minimizing the variational KL.

nodes.name: Expand the bound via factorization
nodes.statement: Use the factorizations of $p$ and $q$ to write $\mathcal{L} = E_q[\log p(\theta\mid\alpha)] + E_q[\log p(\mathbf{z}\mid\theta)] + E_q[\log p(\mathbf{w}\mid\mathbf{z},\beta)] - E_q[\log q(\theta)] - E_q[\log q(\mathbf{z})]$ and substitute the Dirichlet log-expectation identity from Appendix A.1.

nodes.name: Maximize in $\phi_{ni}$ via Lagrangian
nodes.statement: Form the constrained Lagrangian $\mathcal{L}_{[\phi_{ni}]}$ with $\sum_i \phi_{ni}=1$, set $\partial/\partial\phi_{ni}=0$, obtaining $\phi_{ni} \propto \beta_{i v}\exp\{\Psi(\gamma_i) - \Psi(\sum_j \gamma_j)\}$ (Eq. 6).

nodes.name: Maximize in $\gamma_i$
nodes.statement: Collect terms in $\gamma_i$, differentiate, set the derivative to zero; the trigamma terms cancel to yield $\gamma_i = \alpha_i + \sum_{n=1}^N \phi_{ni}$ (Eq. 7). Iterating Eqs. (6) and (7) is required since they are coupled.

nodes.name: Derivation of M-step update for beta
nodes.statement: Isolate the $\beta$-dependent terms in the bound $\mathcal{L}$, add Lagrange multipliers for the row-sum constraints $\sum_j \beta_{ij} = 1$, take the derivative with respect to $\beta_{ij}$ and set to zero to obtain $\beta_{ij} \propto \sum_{d,n} \phi^*_{dni} w^j_{dn}$.

nodes.name: Newton-Raphson update for alpha
nodes.statement: The $\alpha$-portion of the lower bound has Hessian $\partial^2 L/\partial\alpha_i\partial\alpha_j = \delta(i,j)M\Psi'(\alpha_i) - \Psi'(\sum_j \alpha_j)$, of the form $\mathrm{diag}(h) + \mathbf{1}z\mathbf{1}^T$, so the linear-time Newton-Raphson method of Appendix A.2 applies.

nodes.name: Posterior inference for LDA
nodes.statement: Compute $p(\theta, \mathbf{z}\mid\mathbf{w}, \alpha, \beta)$, the posterior over the per-document Dirichlet parameter and topic assignments under LDA. This posterior is intractable in general due to the coupling between $\theta$ and $\beta$ in the topic summation.

nodes.name: Empirical Bayes parameter estimation for LDA
nodes.statement: Given a corpus $\mathcal{D} = \{\mathbf{w}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{w}_M\}$, find $\alpha,\beta$ maximizing the marginal log likelihood $\ell(\alpha,\beta) = \sum_{d=1}^M \log p(\mathbf{w}_d\mid\alpha,\beta)$.

nodes.name: Three-level hierarchical structure
nodes.statement: LDA has corpus-level parameters $\alpha,\beta$ (sampled once per corpus), document-level $\theta_d$ (sampled once per document), and word-level $z_{dn}, w_{dn}$ (sampled per word) — distinguishing it from a two-level Dirichlet-multinomial clustering model.

nodes.name: Continuous mixture of unigrams view
nodes.statement: Marginalizing the topic $z$ in LDA gives a continuous mixture of unigrams $p(\mathbf{w}\mid\alpha,\beta) = \int p(\theta\mid\alpha)\prod_n p(w_n\mid\theta,\beta)\, d\theta$ on the $(V-1)$-simplex with only $k+kV$ parameters yet exhibiting multimodal structure.

nodes.name: Per-iteration complexity of variational inference
nodes.statement: Each iteration of variational inference for LDA requires $O((N+1)k)$ operations; empirically the number of iterations is on the order of $N$, giving roughly $O(N^2 k)$ total operations per document.

nodes.name: Unigram model
nodes.statement: All words drawn i.i.d. from a single multinomial: $p(\mathbf{w}) = \prod_{n=1}^N p(w_n)$.

nodes.name: Mixture of unigrams
nodes.statement: A topic $z$ is drawn for each document then $N$ words are drawn i.i.d. from $p(w\mid z)$: $p(\mathbf{w}) = \sum_z p(z)\prod_{n=1}^N p(w_n\mid z)$. Each document is associated with exactly one topic.

nodes.name: Probabilistic latent semantic indexing (pLSI)
nodes.statement: $p(d, w_n) = p(d)\sum_z p(w_n\mid z) p(z\mid d)$; $d$ is a document index, so the model has $kV + kM$ parameters and is not a well-defined generative model for unseen documents.

nodes.name: TREC AP corpus topic discovery
nodes.statement: 100-topic LDA fit to 16{,}000 TREC AP documents recovers interpretable topics (e.g., Arts, Budgets, Children, Education); per-document variational $\gamma_i - \alpha_i$ identifies which topics generated which words in a held-out article.

nodes.name: Document modeling perplexity comparison
nodes.statement: On the C. Elegans abstracts and TREC AP corpora, LDA achieves lower held-out perplexity than smoothed unigram, smoothed mixture of unigrams, and pLSI (with folding-in) across a range of topic counts $k$.

nodes.name: Reuters-21578 SVM classification with LDA features
nodes.statement: SVMs trained on 50-topic LDA posterior $\gamma^*(\mathbf{w})$ features (a $99.6\%$ feature reduction) match or exceed SVMs trained on raw word features for binary EARN/NOT-EARN and GRAIN/NOT-GRAIN tasks.

nodes.name: EachMovie collaborative filtering
nodes.statement: Predicting a held-out preferred movie for 390 test users from 3300 training users, LDA achieves the best predictive perplexity over a vocabulary of 1600 movies, beating mixture of unigrams and pLSI (folded in).
